exercise.name: Cable Bent Over Single Arm Neutral Grip Kickback with Rope Attachment

reference.title: Cable Bent Over Single Arm Neutral Grip Kickback with Rope Attachment
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching). The schema rope is two-handed, so the one-hand rope end is drawn as a D-handle held with the same neutral grip.

equipment: Rope attachment (one end held; drawn as a D-handle)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you straighten the elbow, inhale as the cable pulls the hand back.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s out, 0.6 s squeeze, about 1.8 s back

prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9). Kickbacks need a light load.
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer squeeze, then one plate on the stack

cues.text: Face a low pulley, feet hip width, knees soft, and hinge forward from the hips with a flat back; left hand on the hip. Hold one rope end in the right hand, palm facing in, upper arm along the side and the elbow bent about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and straighten the elbow, pushing the hand back until the arm is straight along the body.
Squeeze the back of the arm with the arm straight; the upper arm stays still along the trunk.
Breathe in and let the cable bend the elbow slowly back to about 90 degrees.
Keep the back flat and the hips still; repeat, then switch sides.

mistakes.fix: Move slowly and pause with the arm straight; use a lighter load.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arm dropping as the elbow bends
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arm parallel to the trunk throughout.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk rotating open toward the working arm
mistakes.fix: Keep both shoulders square to the pulley.

mistakes.mistake: Rounded back or standing up during the set
mistakes.fix: Hold the hip hinge with a flat back, neck long.
Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees (forearm hanging) to straight (clinical opinion)
Upper arm along the trunk (low shoulder elevation), where the long head carried the most force (Kholinne 2018)
Hip hinge with a flat back, trunk well forward (about 45-60 degrees from vertical) and still (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled with a pause at full extension (clinical opinion); the EMG comparison used sets of 7 reps at 70% of 1RM (Boehler 2011)
Low pulley in front, so the cable pulls the hand forward and keeps tension through the whole range, unlike a dumbbell kickback, which loads mainly near full extension (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Bent Over Single Arm Neutral Grip Kickback with Rope Attachment, video (movement reference)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

cautions: Lower back pain: shorten the hinge, brace, and keep the back flat; stop if form slips (clinical opinion).
Elbow pain: lighter load, slower tempo.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: start light.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Back fatigue: brace the free hand on a bench or the cable column.
Wrist discomfort: keep the palm facing the body (neutral grip, as here).
regressions: Dumbbell kickback supported on a bench.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow against the cable; the load peaks with the arm straight. Kickbacks, dips and triangle push-ups did not differ significantly in long or lateral head EMG and led an eight-exercise comparison (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm near the trunk the long head produced the most force (Kholinne 2018).
